_readme: Approved statements for the print deck: the live game's statements plus the new ones Till approved in the 'Trump or Toddler statements' doc (2026-11-12). id is the web game id where it has one. Edit and run `python3 print/build.py`.

statements.text: Refuses to wear a coat, no matter how cold it is.
“You're not my friend anymore.”
Insists on pressing the elevator button themselves.
“He started it.”
Gets upset when someone else's tower is taller.
“Mine was bigger.”
Everything is either “the best” or “a total disaster”.
“No! I do it!”
Needs a nap after lunch, but will deny being tired.
“Watch me. Watch me. Watch me.”
Only eats food that is beige.
“That's not fair!”
Talks about themselves in the third person.
“Everybody says I'm the best at this.”
Has to be the first one through the door.
Wears diapers.
Announces the same achievement several times a day.
Has tantrums.
Should not be left alone with a phone.
Cannot pronounce your name properly.
Gets louder when asked to be quieter.
Afraid of the vacuum cleaner.
Will not admit to knocking over the lamp.
Needs help with buttons.
Deeply interested in large trucks.
Doesn't like sharing.
Would like a parade.
Throws food.
Has a hairstyle that takes longer than the rest of getting dressed.
Requires a specific cup.
Gives everyone they meet a nickname.
Gets carried when tired.
Has fallen asleep somewhere they were supposed to be paying attention.
Needs constant supervision.
Grabs things that belong to other people.
Can drink a glass of water with one hand all by themself.
Repeats a sentence louder rather than explaining it differently.
Knows almost all letters of the alphabet.
Became an expert on the subject yesterday.
Everyone is happy if they fall asleep early and sleep through the night.
“This mine!”
Wants to be the biggest strongest person in every room.
“I did it. I did it all by myself.”
Has tiny hands.
“I'm not tired!”
Thinks nobody can see them if they cover their eyes.
Needs to hold someone's hand going down the stairs.
Only looks at the pictures, never reads the words.
Has an imaginary friend who agrees with everything they say.
“Nobody knew health care could be so complicated.”
Can count all the way to ten, perfectly.
Learned a new word today and uses it in every sentence.
Knows all the primary colors.
Can put on their own shoes.
Claps for themselves after doing something.
Does not like to eat vegetables.
Waves to everyone from the car window.
Signs their name extra big.
Wants their drawing hung up where everyone can see it.
Is learning to wait their turn.
Can almost tie their own shoelaces.
Is very proud of using the big toilet.
Tells everyone their age, rounded up.
Is learning to eat with a knife and fork.
Likes spinning around in the big chair.
Says “no” before hearing the question.
Builds a wall out of pillows and says nobody is allowed in.
Shouts at the TV.
Wants to be in charge of the remote control.
Wants the bigger piece of cake.
“Again! Again!”
Wants two scoops of ice cream when everyone else gets one.
Wanted to buy the biggest island he could find.
